turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal's data shows foreign direct investment figures for Baja California Sur in 2025.

turns.text: 2025 stands out as the reference year here.

turns.text: So the source is clearly named right there in the portal. It comes from the CNIE inside that guide.

turns.text: The same guide points to employment series stored in the BCS 2050 database.

turns.text: Wait, does it link the investment numbers directly to those employment series? [chuckle]

turns.text: Not yet. This is Radio BCS2050. Today's episode is Portal data · Economy.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The concrete question we will answer is how those investment and employment records actually connect for the state. It is the main point of this episode on the portal data.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal keeps both sets separate for now [pause], so listeners can see what is measured and what remains open. This helps us understand the economy data step by step without jumping to conclusions about jobs or growth.

turns.text: One number at a time helps, right? [chuckle]

turns.text: Yes. First the CNIE investment source, then the employment series from ITAEE and ENOE. That way we can see the documented facts without assuming extra connections between them.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal's thematic guide on economy pulls residential real estate numbers for Baja California Sur straight from the JLL annual report.

turns.text: That report covers 2025.

turns.text: The total volume reached US$1,570 M.

turns.text: The same source counted 1,840 individual units sold.

turns.text: 1,840 homes feels like filling a small town in a single year. [chuckle]

turns.text: Los Cabos alone accounted for US$1,264 M.

turns.text: That share equals 81 percent of the entire state total.

turns.text: The portal lists the source as JLL Reporte Anual Los Cabos 2025.

turns.text: So most of the activity sits in that one corridor.

turns.text: Really? That concentration shows how tightly the market links to one tourism zone.

turns.text: A separate entry from Cabo Real Estate shows US$456 M already under contract in Los Cabos during the second quarter of 2026.

turns.text: That covers 293 units.

turns.text: 293 units under contract already points to steady buyer interest early in the year.

turns.text: The median price listed for those Los Cabos homes sits at US$525,000.

turns.text: US$525,000 is the midpoint price buyers actually paid.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That price point tells us what typical buyers are spending in the main market.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: It also shows how the numbers tie into local construction and service jobs.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The same guide also flags foreign direct investment data for 2025 drawn from the CNIE pack zero seven.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Those investment numbers sit in the portal's economy database alongside employment series.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The employment and economic activity figures come from the Base de datos BCS 2050, using ITAEE and ENOE sources.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal simply stores the series without adding forecasts. [pause]

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So we see the recorded volumes and prices, yet we do not see why certain corridors captured most of the sales.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That leaves open questions about how much of this activity reaches local suppliers and workers.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: What would you ask the real estate offices that reported these numbers?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal's municipal sheets show Los Cabos with 351,111 residents across 428 localities.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That makes it the largest by population, and its 2026 revenue law lists 7421559352 pesos in ingresos.

turns.text: Yes, and the same sheet gives San José del Cabo itself 136,285 people.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Compare that with La Paz municipality at 292,241 residents and 2905974532 pesos in ingresos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal data marks Los Cabos as the primate municipality with the SJD airport and hotel cluster.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Its vocation statement calls it the tourism growth engine and primary international gateway.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Yet the same entry notes aquifers 0317 and 0319 already in deficit.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Now shift south along the Pacific to Todos Santos–El Pescadero.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal describes that area as the amenity spine with culture, residential tourism and creative amenities.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Its strength is a distinct Pacific identity that pulls lifestyle migration.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: But the La Paz ficha flags aquifer 0313 in deficit there too, plus septic and tenure stress.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Further north, Comondú shows 73,021 people and lists Valle Santo Domingo as its agro pole.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Its 2026 ingresos come in at 817244119 pesos, well below the two larger municipalities.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Mulegé sits at 64,022 residents with Santa Rosalía and Guerrero Negro as main centers.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Loreto is the smallest listed at 18,052 people, anchored by the Bahía de Loreto protected area.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The tourism inventory on the portal names five high-end properties, all inside Los Cabos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Esperanza, Chileno Bay, Nobu, Montage and The Cape each carry Auberge or Thompson branding.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That cluster matches the portal's note on brand recognition driving fiscal capacity in the south.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Still, the same Los Cabos sheet lists coastal speculation and peak energy load as constraints.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So the data show clear differences in size, revenue and main economic vocation across the five municipalities.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Comondú lists 589 localities and keeps its planning documents on disk without a public cadastre viewer.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Mulegé has 381 localities and its PMDU stays in consultative process with no public IMPLAN portal.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Loreto holds a 2014 POEL in force along the Nopoló–Puerto Escondido corridor.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: What stands out to you when you lay those five sheets side by side? [pause]

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The water deficits appear in four of the five entries. How do you read that pattern?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal's library holds three key documents on regional economies.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: They are the 2011 Triumph of the City by Edward Glaeser.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Yes, and the 2012 New Geography of Jobs by Enrico Moretti.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Plus the 1999 Spatial Economy by Fujita, Krugman and Venables.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal shows these as core references for thinking about growth in places like Baja California Sur.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Glaeser's book makes the case for urban productivity driven by human capital.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: It explains how dense cities raise wages through better matching of skills and ideas.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Why does that matter here? Because our towns could gain from concentrating talent and services.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Moretti's work adds the idea of innovation-sector multipliers.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: One new tech or design job can support several others in the local economy.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal notes this could support tourism plus diversification in BCS.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Exactly. Relying only on visitors leaves us exposed when seasons shift.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The Fujita, Krugman and Venables volume gives the modeling foundations.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It shows how transport costs and market size shape where industries locate.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That framework helps test what happens when regions invest in ports or roads.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal's foresight archive adds one recent note from the Sea of Cortez Forum.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: It records the forum calling for doubling the regional economy.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: While also flagging limits from coastal erosion and water issues.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So the documents together frame both the growth logic and the constraints we already see.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: What stands out to you in how these sources connect?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: They remind us that productivity gains depend on where people and firms choose to cluster.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: And that choice is shaped by real infrastructure and policy choices today.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Take Glaeser's point on human capital. [chuckle] If skilled workers gather in one spot, wages tend to rise for everyone nearby.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Moretti's multiplier idea feels practical too. One design firm might bring along accountants, cafes and suppliers.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The older spatial model shows why roads and ports matter. Lower transport costs pull activity toward bigger markets.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The Sea of Cortez note from November 16 ties it to our coast. Doubling the economy runs into erosion between Punta Lobos and San Carlos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Right. The documents lay out the theory, yet the archive shows the real limits already recorded.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: What would you ask the forum next time they meet?

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The portal's ontology links project viability directly to water, energy and planning layers.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Exactly. The viability package for any hotel, desaladora or industrial park pulls in DMA figures from CONAGUA's DOF 2023.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Those figures are legal balances under NOM-011, not physical measurements.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Right. Aquifer 0313 Todos Santos shows minus 2.964513 hm³ per year, a deficit inside La Paz municipality.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That number comes straight from the DOF entry, and it stays separate from any nearby balance.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Next to it, aquifer 0314 El Pescadero records a small positive 0.107682 hm³ per year, shared by La Paz and Los Cabos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: But the graph does not let one surplus cancel another deficit. Each aquifer stays independent.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: [chuckle] I keep coming back to that rule whenever someone asks about moving water across lines.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: The same ontology ties these balances to the instruments listed in the 2024 state territorial programme.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Those include the 2018 La Paz urban plan and the 2008 Todos Santos–Pescadero subregional programme.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Any new connection, road or housing node must sit inside those plans or the graph flags a mismatch.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Energy sits beside water. The package checks SIBCS, CFE and PRODESEN layers before marking a project viable.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: For East Cape the scorecard shows two clear gaps: settlement pressure data and local employment numbers.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal notes DMA 0318 and the ANP sit on the graph, yet no quantitative load total appears.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So a developer cannot yet read a single ceiling figure for rooms or jobs from the current knowledge base.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: [pause] The graph therefore marks the evidence as incomplete rather than declaring any project blocked or approved.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That forces anyone checking viability to consult the families and mesas listed under the same ontology node.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The portal keeps those actors and tables connected to the water and planning layers without adding new numbers.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: One practical result is that any East Cape proposal must still clear the existing ANP and coastal restrictions first.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: And the graph will keep showing the missing quantitative load until new CONAGUA or INEGI data arrives.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What part of that chain would you want to trace first if you were reviewing a project file?

turns.text: Did you know the portal's guía temática del portal on economy shows Los Cabos had 15 months of inventory in the second quarter of 2026?

turns.text: 15 months. That feels like a long runway for buyers.

turns.text: Exactly. The same guide lists 2,134 active units on the market, valued at US$2.86 B.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: US$2.86 B. That is a serious stock of properties sitting ready.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It is. [chuckle] Now shift to January 2026 and the same guide gives an average daily rate of US$499.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: US$499 a night. That number alone tells you the price level in the hotels.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Right next to it sits the RevPAR at US$369, drawn from the FITURCA Observatorio data in the guide.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So even with high room rates, the revenue per available room still lands at US$369.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: And passenger arrivals at the Los Cabos airport reached 328.5 thousand that same January.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: 328.5 thousand people in one month. That flow supports the whole hotel side.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: On the housing side the guide pulls from SNIIV and shows 776 new home registrations across Baja California Sur in 2025.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: 776. That is the recorded count for the whole state that year.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The financing line for the same period lists 8,993 actions totaling 6,560 million pesos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: 6,560 million pesos. Those actions and that amount together show how much public support went into new homes.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The guide keeps the two topics side by side, so you can see the tourism numbers next to the housing numbers.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What surprises you most when you line them up like that?

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: The 15 months of inventory still feels like the one that makes you stop and look again. [pause] What would you ask the people tracking these numbers next quarter?

turns.text: The portal's data shows foreign direct investment for BCS in 2025 through the CNIE pack 07.

turns.text: That figure comes from the thematic guide on economy. It records the total but leaves the sectors unclear.

turns.text: It tells us the amount arrived, yet it does not break down tourism or real estate shares.

turns.text: Employment, ITAEE and ENOE appear as time series in the BCS 2050 database.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Those series track job numbers and activity over time. They do not explain what caused the changes.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So we see the trend but not the story behind each up or down.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Exactly. The data gives us the measurement, not the reason.

turns.text: Residential volume in BCS reached US$1,570 M according to the JLL Reporte Anual Los Cabos 2025.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That amount covers the whole state. It counts only finished transactions.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Los Cabos alone accounts for US$1,264 M.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That is 81 percent of the total. The rest sits in other municipalities.

turns.text: The same JLL report lists 1,840 residential units sold in 2025.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: It counts completed sales only. Pre-sales or future projects stay outside this number.

turns.text: Cabo RE data for 2026 Q2 shows US$456 M under contract.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: That covers 293 units. These are agreements, not closed deals yet.

turns.text: The median price in Los Cabos stood at US$525,000 in the same quarter.

turns.text: Active inventory reached 2,134 units.

turns.text: Those units were valued at US$2.86 B.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Supply stood at 15 months. That tells us how long current listings might last at recent sales pace.

turns.text: RevPAR for Los Cabos hit US$369 in January 2026.

turns.text: ADR reached US$499 that month, both from FITURCA Observatorio FEB26.

turns.text: Those two figures measure hotel performance. RevPAR blends occupancy and rate.

turns.text: SJD airport recorded 328.5 thousand passengers in January 2026.

turns.text: Financing reached 8,993 actions and $6,560 M MXN the same year.

turns.text: We have spent this episode looking at the portal data on the economy.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: Right, and how those records from the different layers connect to daily decisions people make here.

turns.text: Exactly. The portal pulls from official sources and shows the state of things without adding any forecasts.

turns.speaker: cohost
turns.text: So when residents look at that information they can see where resources are going and where gaps remain.

turns.text: It changes the conversation from guessing to working with what is actually documented.

turns.text: The records make those connections visible in a way that feels immediate for anyone planning their week.

turns.text: When you see the same sources listed across layers it becomes easier to trace one decision to its effect on a nearby town.
